description: ORIVANTA is a team of passionate and innovative minds driven by technology, creativity, and space exploration. We believe in teamwork, continuous learning, and solving real-world challenges through technology. Our proposed project, ASTROHAB, aims to develop an interactive astronaut survival simulator that explores the challenges of living beyond Earth. We welcome enthusiastic individuals skilled in coding, web development, design, data analysis, and space science.
summary:
LUNAR LOOP is an interactive educational simulation game that challenges players to manage a lunar outpost and keep four astronauts alive for 30 mission days. As mission commander of Artemis Base Alpha, players must balance essential resources, including water, oxygen, food, energy, radiation protection, and crew health.

The game features interconnected resource-management systems, greenhouse food production, resource recycling, and unexpected emergencies such as oxygen leaks and crew morale challenges. Every decision can affect multiple systems, encouraging players to think critically, prioritize resources, and understand the challenges of sustainable lunar living.

Inspired by NASA space exploration and life-support research, LUNAR LOOP makes complex space survival concepts engaging and accessible through interactive gameplay. All in-game numerical values are illustrative and intended for educational purposes.

Team ORIVANTA – Beyond Imagination. Into Discovery.
details:
LUNAR LOOP is an interactive lunar survival simulation designed to make the challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon easier to understand.

The player takes the role of mission commander at Artemis Base Alpha, responsible for keeping four astronauts alive for 30 lunar mission days. Players monitor and manage water, oxygen, food, energy, radiation shielding, crew health and other essential survival systems.

The simulation includes water recycling, oxygen recovery, solar power generation, greenhouse food production and radiation protection. These systems are interconnected, so decisions involving one resource can affect other systems. For example, expanding greenhouse production can improve food availability while increasing the demand for water and energy.

Players also face unexpected emergencies, including oxygen leaks, dust storms and crew morale challenges. They must choose appropriate responses and manage limited resources to keep the crew safe. The game includes a mission briefing, a How to Play guide, an informational note, a mission log and a final mission report with a performance score.

The project is inspired by NASA research and resources related to environmental control and life-support systems, astronaut radiation protection, space farming, lunar exploration and lunar dust. These references are included in the game's NASA References & Credits section. All numerical values are simplified illustrative simulations for educational purposes, not real lunar engineering predictions. LUNAR LOOP is an independent educational project and is not an official NASA product.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with AI-assisted development support from Google Antigravity and ChatGPT. The website is deployed publicly using Netlify.

Our goal is to encourage curiosity about space exploration, develop resource-management and critical-thinking skills, and help students understand the scientific and practical challenges of long-duration lunar missions.
